microsoftGuide.title: How to connect your Microsoft account
microsoftGuide.intro: Follow these steps to link your work Microsoft account so you can send and receive emails within CitizenOne.
microsoftGuide.step1: Click Login via Microsoft above - you will be redirected to the Microsoft sign-in page.
microsoftGuide.step2: Enter your work email address (e.g. yourname(at)yourcompany.com) and password.
microsoftGuide.step3: Complete multi-factor authentication (MFA) if your organisation requires it.
microsoftGuide.step4: On the permissions screen, CitizenOne is requesting access to read and send emails on your behalf. Choose one of the following:
microsoftGuide.step4Accept: Accept - grants access for your own account only. You can start immediately.
microsoftGuide.step4Request: Request approval - if your IT admin has restricted app access, click this to send them an approval request. Return to connect once they have approved it in the Azure Portal.
microsoftGuide.step4Hint: If you are unsure, click Accept. If it fails with a permissions error, contact your IT administrator and ask them to grant admin consent for CitizenOne in your organisation's Azure Active Directory.
microsoftGuide.step5: You will be redirected back to CitizenOne automatically and a success message will confirm the connection.
microsoftGuide.step6: Your inbox is now connected. You can read, reply, forward, and send emails from within CitizenOne.
microsoftGuide.stayConnected: CitizenOne refreshes your connection automatically. You may need to reconnect if you change your Microsoft password, your organisation revokes app access, or your account is disabled in Azure AD.
microsoftGuide.troubleshoot1A: Make sure you are using your work account (not a personal Microsoft account) and that your IT admin has approved CitizenOne.
microsoftGuide.troubleshoot2A: Your browser may have blocked the redirect. Disable popup blockers for this site and try again.
microsoftGuide.troubleshoot3Q: "You don't have permission to access this"
microsoftGuide.troubleshoot3A: Your IT administrator needs to grant admin consent for CitizenOne in your organisation's Azure portal.

profile.title: What is this?
profile.body: Your own details and how you are notified. Changes here apply to your user only, not to your colleagues.

company.title: What are company settings?
company.body: Your company details, security and which modules are switched on. It applies to everyone in the company.

import.title: What can be imported?
import.body: Load data from a spreadsheet or another system instead of typing it in again. Run a test import first.

subscription.title: What is the subscription?
subscription.body: Your current plan and what it costs. This is also where you buy extra users and departments.

invoices.title: What is listed here?
invoices.body: Every invoice from CitizenOne. A paid invoice is your receipt and can be forwarded to your bookkeeper.

licenses.title: What are licences?
licenses.body: How many seats you have bought and who uses them. Remove a licence from an employee to free the seat.

storage.title: What is taking up space?
storage.body: How much room your files use and what takes the most. Buy more space, or clear out the largest files.

portalAccess.title: What is portal access?
portalAccess.body: Decides what relatives, third parties and services can see in their own portal. Anything you switch on becomes visible to them.

activityLogs.title: What is logged?
activityLogs.body: Who signed in and what they did. Use it to document access to personal data.

timeLogs.title: What are time logs?
timeLogs.body: Working time recorded by your staff. Use it as the basis for payroll and to follow up on shifts.

mileageLog.title: What is the mileage log?
mileageLog.body: Journeys recorded by your staff, ready for reimbursement or bookkeeping.

supportAccess.title: Why this page?
supportAccess.body: Here you decide whether CitizenOne support may see your data, and you can see when they have. Access closes itself.

gdprRetention.title: What is retention?
gdprRetention.body: How long data is kept before it is deleted automatically. Set the limits to match your own deletion policy.

smsNotifications.title: What is SMS?
smsNotifications.body: Send messages by text as well as by email. Usage is billed by the number of messages sent.

powerBi.title: What does Power BI do?
powerBi.body: Pull your data into reports in Power BI. The key grants read access, not the right to change anything.

economic.title: What does e-conomic do?
economic.body: Send invoices and vouchers on to your accounting system, so the figures are only typed once.

fst.title: What is FindSocialeTilbud.dk?
fst.body: Show your services on FindSocialeTilbud.dk so municipalities can find you. You decide what is published.

customPages.title: What is the glossary?
customPages.body: Your own words for fields and pages. Rename a field so the system calls it what you call it.

transactions.title: What are transactions?
transactions.body: Money in and out of the accounts you keep for each person. The amounts can be exported to your bookkeeper.

roles.title: What are roles?
roles.body: A role decides which pages and actions an employee can reach. Grant too little rather than too much.

departments.title: What are departments?
departments.body: Departments decide who sees what, and are used in schedules, reports and access.

employeeGroups.title: What are employee groups?
employeeGroups.body: Put staff into groups so you can assign shifts, tasks and access to several at once.

archived.title: What is the archive?
archived.body: Everything you archived instead of deleting. It can be brought back and stays out of your daily view.

access.title: What is this for?
access.body: These lists decide how you are organised and who may do what. They fill fields all over the system.

communication.title: What is this for?
communication.body: Templates and setup for the messages you send, so the text is not written from scratch every time.

journal.title: What is this for?
journal.body: These lists fill in the journal's own fields: titles, content, tags and consents.

health.title: What is this for?
health.body: Medicines, units and templates that staff choose from when they document health.

schedule.title: What is this for?
schedule.body: Shift types, absence, norm periods and supplements that the schedule and time accounts calculate from.

booking.title: What is this for?
booking.body: Rooms and labels that the calendar and bookings choose from.

citizens.title: What is this for?
citizens.body: The lists behind the record: relationships, addresses, categories and inquiries.

employment.title: What is this for?
employment.body: Setup for jobcentre work: agreements, case types, statuses and billing.

customLinks.title: What are custom links?
customLinks.body: Add shortcuts to the left sidebar - like your intranet, a shared drive, a booking system or any external tool your team uses. Choose whether each link is shown to admins, users or everyone.

movedNotice.title: We have tidied up in here
